reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer, wide-packet re-review batch 3, 2026-08-01

samples_reviewed.question_text: What time does the clock show?
What time does the clock show?
Look at the July 2025 calendar. What day of the week is July 17?
Look at the May 2025 calendar. What day of the week is May 14?
What time does the clock show?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Not one of the 6 samples computes a duration in days or weeks; seeds 42, 43, and 46 are plain clock-reading ('What time does the clock show?'), seeds 44 and 45 ask only a single day-of-week lookup ('What day of the week is July 17?'), and seed 51 is clock-setting.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The competency's core phrase 'duration of an event in terms of number of days and/or weeks' never appears; there is no 'how many days between July 3 and July 17' or 'how many weeks did the event last' item anywhere in the 6-sample packet.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The calendar day-of-week lookups at seeds 44 and 45 ('Look at the July 2025 calendar. What day of the week is July 17?') are grade-appropriate reading tasks, but they demand a different, simpler skill than the multi-step subtraction reasoning a duration-in-days problem requires.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The six samples split into clock-time reading (42, 43, 46), calendar day-lookup (44, 45), and clock-setting (51) -- three unrelated skills, none of which is the duration-counting task the competency names.

competency_alignment.rationale: The sampled variation moves along a 'tell/set time on a clock' axis (11:00, 1:00, 2:00, 4:00) rather than the 'count days/weeks on a calendar' axis this competency is actually about.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Since no sample ever states a start and end date or event span, there is no observable duration magnitude in days or weeks to judge against the competency at all.
